title: JRC ASAP ten-daily warnings of agricultural vegetation anomalies (sub-national, since 2001)
description: Automatic warnings about low or delayed vegetation performance for crops and rangelands, issued every dekad (10 days) for first-level administrative units worldwide by the European Commission Joint Research Centre's ASAP system (Anomaly hotspots of Agricultural Production). Warning levels 1–4 combine rainfall and vegetation-index anomalies during the active growing season; units are also flagged as off season or as having no significant crop/rangeland. The complete history since the last dekad of May 2001 is published as a CSV, with a second-level version for selected countries and the latest warnings as WFS/WMS layers.
purpose: Provides an independent, long, dekadal record of agricultural drought warnings for each of Algeria's 48 (pre-2019) wilayas, useful to compare with AEO drought indices and with cereal production statistics.

spatial_extent.description: Global, at ASAP first-level units (gaul1_asap, adapted from FAO GAUL); join on asap1_id with the gaul1_asap_v06 shapefile. Algeria (asap0_id 54) has 48 units named after the 48 wilayas of the pre-2019 division, for example Adrar, Tipaza, Setif and Tamanrasset. Users filter the global CSV by country.

temporal_extent.description: From the last dekad of May 2001 to present: 917 dekads from 2001-05-21 to 2026-11-01 in the file downloaded on 2026-11-22 (file dated 21 November 2026). Warnings are published 2–3 days after the end of each dekad.

resolution.spatial: first-level administrative units (Algeria: 48 wilayas, pre-2019 division)

variables.name: asap0_id, asap1_id, asap0_name, asap1_name
variables.description: Country and first-level unit codes and names (join keys for gaul0_asap / gaul1_asap)

variables.name: w_crop, w_crop_na, w_crop_de, w_crop_gr
variables.description: Crop warning code, short name, long description and warning group (No warning, Warning group 1–4, Off season, No crop/rangeland)

processing: Every dekad, ASAP computes rainfall (e.g. SPI-3), water-balance and vegetation-index anomaly indicators over the crop and rangeland areas of each unit, using a remote-sensing phenology to determine whether the season is active, and assigns a warning level from the share of the active area affected (e.g. 'at least 25 % of the active area is affected by an anomaly for the indicator SPI 3'). The classification scheme is documented in the ASAP warning classification v8.0 report.
validation: Not assessed on the pages consulted; Rembold et al. (2019) describe the system design.
limitations: Units are Algeria's 48 pre-2019 wilayas, not the current wilaya division; results must be re-mapped before comparison with current wilaya statistics.
Automatic warnings, not production estimates; Saharan units without significant crop or rangeland (e.g. Adrar) are coded 99 and off-season dekads 98.
The classification has been revised over time (current scheme v8.0) and indicator inputs have changed; check whether past dekads were reprocessed before analysing long-term frequencies.
The global CSV is large (48.6 MB zipped, about 900 MB unzipped, 3.39 million rows).

algeria_notes: The downloaded file holds 44,016 Algerian rows (48 units × 917 dekads). Over the full record, crop codes were dominated by 'Off season' (11,570 rows), 'No warning' (code 0: 9,562; codes 10 and 20 also map to the 'No warning' group) and 'No crop/rangeland' (9,170, Saharan units), with 1,978 rows in warning group 2 and 1,039 in group 4. For the dekad of 2026-11-01, Tipaza had a level-1 crop warning (SPI-3 anomaly on at least 25 % of the active area).
